1.explanation: The OverflowMenu component’s static propTypes includes a deprecate() validator on the `light` prop, causing a warning whenever PropTypes are checked—even when the user never passed `light`. In addition, defaultProps typically provides a default value for `light`, which means the deprecation validator runs on every render. To fix the bug, the propTypes entry for `light` must be adjusted (or removed) so it only warns when the user explicitly supplies the prop, and/or the defaultProps entry for `light` should be removed so the deprecation check isn’t triggered by the default value.
1.bug_scenario: The user renders an <OverflowMenu> with two <OverflowMenuItem> children and does not set the deprecated “light” prop, but nevertheless sees the console warning “The `light` prop for `OverflowMenu` is no longer needed and has been deprecated…”. This unexpected warning is breaking their tests, which fail on any console warning even if they didn’t explicitly set that prop.

2.explanation: The deprecation warning is injected by the custom `deprecate` validator in the OverflowMenu component’s propTypes for the `light` prop. Even though the user never sets `light`, the validator is still run (possibly because `defaultProps.light` is defined or the prop is always present), causing the warning unconditionally. To fix this, the `light` propType should only call the `deprecate` warning when the prop is explicitly provided (e.g. by checking `props.hasOwnProperty('light')`) or remove any default value so that `deprecate` does not fire when the prop is omitted.
2.bug_scenario: The user renders an OverflowMenu without ever passing a `light` prop, yet a deprecation warning for the `light` prop still appears in the console. The screenshot shows the warning: “The `light` prop for `OverflowMenu` is no longer needed and has been deprecated…”. This warning breaks test suites that fail on unexpected console warnings.
